subject: Private Upgrade Proposal — snapshot-first rollback & narrow-window cadence
messages:

Subject: Private Upgrade Proposal — snapshot-first rollback & narrow-window cadence

Hi Jamal / Sparrow ops team,

Following our runbook review last week, attached is a condensed plan for the Private cluster upgrade we discussed. This is intentionally conservative and centers on a "snapshot-first" rollback approach so you have a fast, low-risk revert option rather than relying solely on multi-step application downgrades. High-level summary: 

- Proposed window: 2026-07-13 02:00–04:00 UTC (narrow maintenance window to minimize business-hours impact).
- Rollout model: staged canary across 3 tranches (10% → 40% → 100%) with at least 30m steady-state after canary.
- Rollback primary: restore LVM/ZFS snapshot of node (snapshot-first) plus service pin reversion. Secondary rollback: model/service image re-pin to prior immutable tag.
- State handling: full KV cache dump prior to first tranche; warmers to rebuild cache post-upgrade. Snapshotting includes hot DB logical backups where available (per your infra constraints).
- Network quiesce plan: soft quiesce via connection drain + BGP withdrawal for affected subnets (we avoid VLAN moves where possible).
- Health gates: 0% error-rate increase for critical endpoints, token latency SLO +-20% compared to baseline, canary smoke tests in attached checklist.

Attachments: private-upgrade-runbook.md (step-by-step), upgrade-matrix.xlsx (node-to-image mapping), canary-smoke-checklist.txt.

Can you confirm the window works on your side? Also flag any constraints on snapshot duration or cross-datacenter snapshot replication — if snapshots take >10min we should extend the canary gap.

Thanks,
Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

Subject: Re: Private Upgrade Proposal — snapshot-first rollback & narrow-window cadence

Neha — thanks for the clear plan. A few quick clarifications from ops: 

1) Our on-prem storage uses ZFS snapshots but replication to DR is async and can lag ~20–30m during peak. Will that affect the snapshot-first rollback assumption?
2) Can you confirm whether the KV cache dump is a point-in-time export or a live stream? We need to coordinate with our cache team to ensure memory limits.
3) Network team prefers not to withdraw BGP unless strictly required — can we do a connection-drain-only first, then conditional BGP withdraw if traffic doesn't drop?

Also: the proposed window (02:00–04:00 UTC) is okay but we'd like to start earlier (01:30 UTC) if the snapshot step looks like it may take >10min. Can your on-call accommodate a 30m buffer?

Jamal
Director, Platform Engineering
SparrowPayments

Thanks Jamal — good questions. Short answers and some updated notes inline below.

1) ZFS replication lag: noted. Snapshot-first still valid as a local revert (fast), but DR replacement will lag. We'll treat DR as eventual recovery not primary rollback; plan updated to include local snapshot restore in <5–10m for a single node, and a follow-up DR replication job after we confirm cluster health. I've added a contingency that if replication lag >20m, we hold on full-cluster rollout until post-window. See runbook section 4.2.

2) KV cache: we intend to create a point-in-time export (local dump) before the first tranche. The dump is a compact snapshot (not a live stream). We'll coordinate with your cache maintainers to place the dump on a shared NFS mount for faster restore. Estimated dump time for your current dataset: 3–6 minutes (per matrix).

3) Network quiesce: agreed — switch primary action to connection drain + application-level fallbacks. BGP withdrawal moved to an emergency-only step in the network playbook. Updated in runbook.

Window buffer: we can shift the start to 01:30 UTC and still finish under your constraints. I'll have Karthik on the bridge for orchestration; Soojin will own canary smoke validations and rollback triggers.

Next steps (action items):
- Jamal/ops: confirm 01:30–04:00 UTC window and on-site NTP/snapshot hang checks (by EOD 2026-07-07).
- Redwood: we'll provide a tagged bootstrap image and the final upgrade-matrix.xlsx with node IDs and expected snapshot sizes (by 2026-07-09).
- Ops: provide contact for cache team and confirmation of NFS writable path.

We kept the rollback criteria intentionally strict: any >2% sustained error increase on critical endpoints for 10min triggers immediate rollback. That’s in the checklist.

Neha

All — I can be on-call for the 01:30–04:00 UTC window. A couple of operational notes from the orchestration side: 

- We'll implement a node pin check before each tranche to ensure no accidental drift; the pin will be an immutable image tag and we keep the previous tag staged for immediate redeploy.
- During canary we will funnel traffic via the service router to only the canary nodes. If a rollback is triggered we will (1) stop traffic to the tranche, (2) restore node snapshot, (3) re-attach KV dump and run warmers, then (4) run the smoke checklist. The whole restore path is scripted in the runbook and measured in our testbed at ~8–12 min end-to-end for a single node.
- I'll publish a short run-of-show in the bridge chat 24h before the window.

Sooj, Neha — I left the canary validation thresholds in the checklist; happy to tighten if Sparrow wants lower tolerance.

Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
